item.title: galore
item.description:
Merriam-Webster's Word of the Day for October 11, 2026 is:

galore • \guh-LOR\  • adjective

Galore is an informal adjective that describes something as being in large numbers or amounts. It is always used postpositively, that is, after a noun.

// The store promises bargains galore on Black Friday.

See the entry >

Examples:

“The rest of the home is filled with what Josh calls ‘love stuff,’ like an entire wall of family pictures, his mother’s recipe box, random heirlooms, and artwork galore, including his grandfather’s acid etching prints and three-dimensional pieces made by his mother … who worked in wood and papier-mâché.” — Meg McConahey, The Mercury News (San Jose, California), 1 July 2026

Did you know?

Galore means “in large numbers or amounts,” making it a synonym of useful words like abundant and plentiful.

item.title: Luddite
item.description:
Luddite • \LUH-dyte\  • noun

Luddite refers to someone who is opposed to change, and especially to technological change.
